messages.content: Hi! How can I help you today?

Hello, I’m having trouble sending those picture messages—MMS, I think they’re called? It’s been a few hours now and they just won’t go through. I’m not very good with these things, so I’d really appreciate some help to get it working again.
Sure, I can help with that. To get started, could you please provide the phone number associated with the line you’re trying to send MMS from?
Oh, yes, of course. My phone number is 555-123-2002.

Let’s walk through a few checks to get MMS working again.  

1. Verify basic cellular & data service  
   • Can you place a normal voice call right now?  
   • Can you load a webpage in your browser (with mobile data, not Wi-Fi)?  

2. Ensure you’re on at least a 3G/4G network  
   • In your phone’s Settings → Mobile Networks → Network mode, choose “4G/5G preferred” (or similar).  

3. Check your APN’s MMSC URL  
   • Go to Settings → Mobile Networks → Access Point Names (APNs)  
   • Tap your carrier’s APN and look for “MMSC” (Multimedia Messaging Service Center).  
   • If it’s blank or looks wrong, tap the menu and select “Reset to default.”  

4. Reboot your phone  
   • After resetting the APN, power off and on so the new settings take effect.  

5. Disable Wi-Fi Calling (if enabled)  
   • In Settings → Connections → Wi-Fi Calling, turn it OFF.  

6. Verify Messaging app permissions  
   • In Settings → Apps → Messaging → Permissions, make sure Storage and SMS permissions are allowed.  

Please work through those steps and let me know at which point things improve (or if any setting doesn’t look right). Once we narrow it down, we can take the next action.

Oh my, that’s quite a list! I get a bit lost with all these steps. Could we maybe start with just the first one? I’m not sure how to check if I can load a webpage with mobile data—do I need to turn off my Wi-Fi for that? And will doing any of this mess up my photos or anything important on my phone?

No worries—this first check is very safe and won’t touch your photos or delete anything. Here’s how to do it step by step:

1. Test a voice call  
   • Open your Phone app and dial any number you know works (for example, a friend or your voicemail, often by holding “1”).  
   • If the call connects and you hear ringing or your voicemail greeting, your cellular service is up.

2. Test mobile data in your browser  
   • Yes—if you’re connected to Wi-Fi, your phone will use that instead of cellular data. To force a mobile-data test, just turn Wi-Fi off first:  
     – Swipe down from the top of your screen to open Quick Settings.  
     – Tap the Wi-Fi icon so it’s grayed out (OFF).  
   • Open your web browser and try loading any simple website, like “example.com” or “google.com.”  
   • If the page loads, your mobile data is working. If it fails to load, your data connection may be off or blocked.

Please try those two steps and let me know:  
• Did the test call go through?  
• Were you able to load a webpage after turning Wi-Fi off?  

That will tell us if basic service and data are OK before we move on.
